source.credit: Duxbury et al. (2004), Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets 109, E02002

constraints.axisConvention: Full axes are halved exactly. +Z is the adopted pole; +X is the arbitrary display meridian.
constraints.qualification: Published preliminary ellipsoid using minimum full dimensions from Stardust flyby images. It does not reproduce the observed angular outline or establish a complete global shape.
constraints.scale: The reference radius is the geometric mean of the approximation semiaxes. It is a rendering scale, not an independent measured mean radius or convex-model volume.

assumptions: Published preliminary ellipsoid using minimum full dimensions from Stardust flyby images. It does not reproduce the observed angular outline or establish a complete global shape.
Arbitrary display pole and meridian. The flyby did not establish a spin pole or current surface longitude; the display orientation is not a measured attitude.
approximation.qualification: Observation-constrained ellipsoid; no invented local terrain or albedo.

spin.meaning: Arbitrary display pole and meridian. The flyby did not establish a spin pole or current surface longitude; the display orientation is not a measured attitude.

unresolved: Original closed scientific mesh and registered surface mosaic were not located in the checked Stardust archive.
The reported 6.6 × 5.0 × 3.4 km dimensions are minimum extents from limited viewing, not three exact global axis measurements.
The real body has angular surfaces that this preliminary ellipsoid does not reproduce.
Neither the arbitrary display pole nor its zero meridian is an observed physical orientation.
